name: ptyper2-par1-scala-order
description: As `ptyper2-par1-scala`, with the one-worker path made to do the serial typer's work in the serial typer's order: `-Dscalac.parallelTyper.order=source` (units in source order), `lazySignatures` (no signatures pre-pass) and `noForceLazyVals` (no forcing of the definitions' lazy vals). With these the spike reports pickles byte-identical to serial on the library, so `par1` against `spike` here is the cost of the concurrent implementations alone, and the difference from `ptyper2-par1-scala` is what the driver's order does. xctrace counts the benchmark thread only: compare the `-Yparallel-typer` variants by time.

variantDescriptions.spike: the parallel typer spike at `3c72e64ddf`, without `-Yparallel-typer`
variantDescriptions.aa: the first variant's build again, in its own class loader: the A/A
